mergedParams.userDescription: Old film grain and dusty overlays. internal effects for text, video, images

prompts.prompt: Create an internal effect preset called 'FilmGrainOverlay' that adds animated film grain and dust particles to any component. The effect should use multiple layered opacity animations with random noise patterns to simulate authentic vintage film degradation. Include parameters for grain intensity (0-1), dust frequency (low/medium/high), and age level (subtle/moderate/heavy). The effect should create a flickering opacity overlay that varies between 0.02-0.15 opacity with rapid keyframe changes every 0.05 seconds to simulate grain movement. Add occasional dust specks as brief opacity spikes (0.3-0.5) that appear randomly throughout the duration. Use a combination of brightness and contrast filters that subtly pulse to simulate projector light variations. The effect should be applicable to any component type (text, video, or image) via targetIds.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Effect type: Generic (AnimationRange[]). Create three separate effects in the return array: 1) Primary grain effect with opacity AnimationRange cycling between {prog:0, val:0.05}, {prog:0.1, val:0.12}, {prog:0.2, val:0.08} etc. with 20+ keyframes for grain texture. 2) Dust speck effect with occasional opacity spikes at random prog values. 3) Brightness filter effect with subtle variations between 0.95-1.05. Use provider mode with targetIds. Input schema: z.object({ intensity: z.number().min(0).max(1), dustFrequency: z.enum(['low', 'medium', 'high']), ageLevel: z.enum(['subtle', 'moderate', 'heavy']), duration: z.number(), targetIds: z.array(z.string()) }). Return format: { effects: [grainEffect, dustEffect, brightnessEffect] }. PresetMetadata: { _internalPreset: true, _internalPresetOutput: 'effects' }

prompts.prompt: Build an internal effect preset named 'VintageFilmFlicker' that simulates old projector flicker and frame instability. This should create a combination of subtle position shifts, intermittent brightness drops, and occasional color desaturation to mimic damaged film reels. The effect should include micro-movements (translateY variations of ±2-5px) that happen irregularly to simulate film gate wobble. Add periodic brightness dips (dropping to 0.7-0.8) that last 0.1-0.2 seconds to simulate projector bulb fluctuations. Include a sepia tone color filter that fades in and out with varying intensity. Parameters should control flicker rate (slow/normal/fast), wobble amount (subtle/moderate/extreme), and color aging (none/sepia/faded). The effect should work seamlessly with video, image, and text atoms.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Effect type: Combined (Generic + Filter effects). Return 4 effects: 1) TranslateY wobble with AnimationRange: [{prog:0, val:0}, {prog:0.15, val:-3}, {prog:0.3, val:2}, {prog:0.45, val:-4}...] continuing with irregular patterns. 2) Brightness flicker with sudden dips: [{prog:0, val:1}, {prog:0.2, val:1}, {prog:0.21, val:0.75}, {prog:0.23, val:1}...]. 3) Sepia filter effect using CSS filter with hue-rotate and sepia values. 4) Subtle scale effect (0.995-1.005) for frame instability. Provider mode targeting. Input schema: z.object({ flickerRate: z.enum(['slow', 'normal', 'fast']), wobbleAmount: z.enum(['subtle', 'moderate', 'extreme']), colorAging: z.enum(['none', 'sepia', 'faded']), duration: z.number().default(5), targetIds: z.array(z.string()) }). PresetMetadata: { _internalPreset: true, _internalPresetOutput: 'effects' }

prompts.prompt: Design an internal effect preset 'ScratchedFilmTexture' that overlays animated scratches, hair, and film damage marks. Create dynamic scratch lines that move vertically across the screen using animated clip-path or mask properties. The scratches should appear as thin semi-transparent white lines (opacity 0.3-0.6) that travel from top to bottom at varying speeds. Include static hair and fiber elements that stick to random positions for 1-2 seconds before disappearing. Add burn marks as dark spots with feathered edges that briefly appear with high opacity (0.7-0.9) then fade. Parameters include scratch density (1-10 scratches), scratch speed (slow/medium/fast), damage level (light/medium/heavy), and whether to include burn marks (boolean). The effect should layer multiple scratch animations with different timing offsets.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Effect type: Generic with complex AnimationRange patterns. Create dynamic array of effects based on scratch density parameter. Each scratch effect uses translateY from -100% to 100% with varying duration (1-3s based on speed param). Scratch opacity animates: [{prog:0, val:0}, {prog:0.1, val:0.4}, {prog:0.9, val:0.4}, {prog:1, val:0}]. Hair elements use static positioning with opacity fade: [{prog:0, val:0}, {prog:0.05, val:0.3}, {prog:0.8, val:0.3}, {prog:1, val:0}]. Burn marks use scale and opacity: scale from 0 to 1.2 to 1, opacity from 0 to 0.8 to 0. Input schema: z.object({ scratchDensity: z.number().min(1).max(10), scratchSpeed: z.enum(['slow', 'medium', 'fast']), damageLevel: z.enum(['light', 'medium', 'heavy']), includeBurns: z.boolean(), duration: z.number(), targetIds: z.array(z.string()) }). Return format: { effects: [...dynamically generated scratch effects] }

prompts.prompt: Develop an internal waveform effect preset 'AudioReactiveFilmDamage' that synchronizes film degradation effects with audio beats. When bass hits occur, trigger brief film tears (scale distortion 1.0 to 1.15 to 1.0). Mid-frequency peaks should cause color bleeding effects (saturate filter 100% to 150% to 100%). Treble spikes trigger dust particle opacity bursts. The effect should feel like the film is physically reacting to sound vibrations, with damage intensifying during loud passages. Include sensitivity controls for each frequency band (bass/mid/treble sensitivity 0-1), damage style (tear/burn/scratch), and reaction speed (instant/smooth/delayed). The vintage aesthetic should make it seem like an old film reel is being affected by speaker vibrations.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Effect type: Waveform (audio-reactive). Create 3 waveform effects: 1) Bass-triggered scale distortion: { type: 'scale', audioProperty: 'bass', sensitivity: params.bassSensitivity, threshold: 0.6, minValue: 1.0, maxValue: 1.15, smoothing: 0.2 }. 2) Mid-frequency saturation: { type: 'custom', audioProperty: 'mid', sensitivity: params.midSensitivity, customProperty: 'filter', filterType: 'saturate', minValue: '100%', maxValue: '150%' }. 3) Treble dust bursts: { type: 'opacity', audioProperty: 'treble', sensitivity: params.trebleSensitivity, threshold: 0.7, minValue: 0, maxValue: 0.4, attackTime: 0.05, releaseTime: 0.3 }. Input schema: z.object({ bassSensitivity: z.number().min(0).max(1), midSensitivity: z.number().min(0).max(1), trebleSensitivity: z.number().min(0).max(1), damageStyle: z.enum(['tear', 'burn', 'scratch']), reactionSpeed: z.enum(['instant', 'smooth', 'delayed']), targetIds: z.array(z.string()) }). PresetMetadata: { _internalPreset: true, _internalPresetOutput: 'effects', dependencies: { hooks: ['useWaveformData'] } }

prompts.prompt: Create an internal effect preset 'FilmProjectorGate' that simulates the mechanical aspects of film projection. Add a subtle vignette effect that pulses slightly to mimic the projector gate opening. Include sprocket hole shadows that briefly appear at the edges as dark rectangular shapes moving vertically. Create a gate weave effect where the entire frame shifts horizontally by 1-3 pixels in a slow, irregular pattern. Add intermittent focus breathing where blur increases from 0 to 2px and back. Parameters should control gate stability (stable/loose/worn), vignette intensity (0-1), sprocket visibility (none/subtle/visible), and focus drift (none/minimal/moderate). The effect should make content feel like it's being physically projected through vintage equipment.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Effect type: Generic with multiple coordinated effects. Create 5 effects: 1) Vignette using radial-gradient background with opacity animation: [{prog:0, val:0.2}, {prog:0.5, val:0.25}, {prog:1, val:0.2}]. 2) Sprocket shadows as translateY animations on edge elements: vertical movement from -100vh to 100vh over 2s intervals. 3) Gate weave using translateX: [{prog:0, val:0}, {prog:0.3, val:2}, {prog:0.6, val:-1}, {prog:1, val:0}] with ease-in-out. 4) Focus breathing with blur filter: [{prog:0, val:0}, {prog:0.25, val:1.5}, {prog:0.5, val:0}, {prog:0.75, val:2}, {prog:1, val:0}]. 5) Subtle rotation for gate instability: ±0.1deg variations. Input schema: z.object({ gateStability: z.enum(['stable', 'loose', 'worn']), vignetteIntensity: z.number().min(0).max(1), sprocketVisibility: z.enum(['none', 'subtle', 'visible']), focusDrift: z.enum(['none', 'minimal', 'moderate']), duration: z.number(), targetIds: z.array(z.string()) }). PresetMetadata: { _internalPreset: true, _internalPresetOutput: 'effects' }

prompts.prompt: Build an internal effect preset 'ChemicalFilmDecay' that simulates chemical degradation of old film stock. Create color shift animations that cycle through subtle hue rotations to mimic color fading and chemical reactions. Add patches of exposure bloom where brightness suddenly increases in random areas (using radial gradient masks). Include vinegar syndrome effects with warping distortions using scale and skew transforms. Implement silver mirroring as metallic sheen overlays with animated linear gradients. Parameters include decay age (new/aged/ancient), chemical type (vinegar/silver/color-fade), intensity (0-1), and bloom frequency. The effect should create an organic, deteriorating appearance that varies across the frame.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Effect type: Generic with advanced filter combinations. Return array of 4 effects: 1) Hue rotation animation: [{prog:0, val:0}, {prog:0.33, val:15}, {prog:0.66, val:-10}, {prog:1, val:0}] applied as filter hue-rotate. 2) Exposure bloom using brightness filter with localized spikes: [{prog:0.2, val:1}, {prog:0.21, val:1.4}, {prog:0.25, val:1}...] at random intervals. 3) Warping via combined scaleX/scaleY with slight variations: scaleX animates 1.0-1.02-1.0, scaleY animates 1.0-0.98-1.0, creating subtle distortion. 4) Silver mirroring as animated linear-gradient overlay with metallic colors (#C0C0C0 to transparent) moving across frame. Input schema: z.object({ decayAge: z.enum(['new', 'aged', 'ancient']), chemicalType: z.enum(['vinegar', 'silver', 'color-fade']), intensity: z.number().min(0).max(1), bloomFrequency: z.number().min(0).max(10), duration: z.number(), targetIds: z.array(z.string()) }). PresetMetadata: { _internalPreset: true, _internalPresetOutput: 'effects' }

prompts.prompt: Design an internal effect preset 'FilmReelEnd' that recreates the classic end-of-reel effects seen in old projectors. Start with stable playback, then add increasing gate jump (sudden vertical shifts), flash frames (white opacity bursts), countdown/leader marks (circular overlays), and final burn-through (expanding white circle from center). The effect should progress through phases: stable (0-60%), unstable (60-80%), critical (80-95%), and burnout (95-100%). Include parameters for reel condition (good/worn/damaged), burn intensity (0-1), include leader marks (boolean), and flash frequency. This creates a dramatic ending effect perfect for transitions or scene endings.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Effect type: Generic with phase-based AnimationRange progressions. Create 5 phase-dependent effects: 1) Gate jump with increasing translateY variations: early phase [{prog:0.6, val:0}, {prog:0.61, val:-10}, {prog:0.62, val:0}], late phase larger jumps up to ±50px. 2) Flash frames as opacity bursts: starting at prog:0.7 with increasing frequency, opacity spikes from 0 to 0.9. 3) Leader marks as circular shape overlays appearing at prog:0.8-0.9. 4) Burn-through effect using radial scale from center: [{prog:0.95, val:0}, {prog:0.98, val:3}, {prog:1, val:5}] with white color. 5) Overall brightness increase towards end: [{prog:0, val:1}, {prog:0.9, val:1.2}, {prog:1, val:2}]. Input schema: z.object({ reelCondition: z.enum(['good', 'worn', 'damaged']), burnIntensity: z.number().min(0).max(1), includeLeaderMarks: z.boolean(), flashFrequency: z.number().min(0).max(10), duration: z.number().default(3), targetIds: z.array(z.string()) }). Return format: { effects: [...phase-based effect array] }

prompts.prompt: Develop an internal effect preset 'DustParticleSystem' that generates a dynamic dust and particle overlay system. Create multiple layers of particles with different sizes, opacities, and movement patterns. Small dust motes should drift slowly downward with slight horizontal wobble. Larger particles should fall faster with rotation. Include floating fiber animations that move horizontally across frame. Add static dust accumulation that builds up over time in corners and edges. Parameters control particle density (sparse/moderate/heavy), particle size range (fine/mixed/coarse), movement speed (slow/normal/fast), and accumulation (boolean). The system should feel organic and three-dimensional with parallax-like depth.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Effect type: Generic with dynamically generated particle effects. Generate array of 10-30 particle effects based on density parameter. Each particle has: 1) Unique translateY animation with duration based on size (larger = faster fall). 2) TranslateX wobble: [{prog:0, val:0}, {prog:0.25, val:randomX}, {prog:0.5, val:-randomX}, {prog:0.75, val:randomX}, {prog:1, val:0}]. 3) Rotation for larger particles: 0 to 360deg over duration. 4) Opacity variations: small particles 0.2-0.4, large particles 0.3-0.6. 5) Scale based on particle size parameter. Static accumulation uses opacity fade-in: [{prog:0, val:0}, {prog:0.7, val:0}, {prog:1, val:0.3}] for corner/edge elements. Input schema: z.object({ particleDensity: z.enum(['sparse', 'moderate', 'heavy']), particleSize: z.enum(['fine', 'mixed', 'coarse']), movementSpeed: z.enum(['slow', 'normal', 'fast']), includeAccumulation: z.boolean(), duration: z.number(), targetIds: z.array(z.string()) }). Use staggered start times for natural flow.

prompts.prompt: Create an internal effect preset 'FilmPerforationDamage' that simulates damage to film sprocket holes affecting playback stability. When perforations are damaged, the film jumps, skips frames, and loses registration. Create sudden vertical jumps combined with brief black frames (opacity 0), horizontal shifts when film loses lateral guide, and rotation wobbles when film isn't held flat. Include tension variations that cause speed changes (scale pulsing). Parameters include damage severity (minor/moderate/severe), damage type (tears/stretching/missing), frequency of jumps (0-10 per second), and registration loss (stable/loose/erratic). The effect should feel mechanical and abrupt, like physical film transport problems.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Effect type: Generic with abrupt, non-eased transitions. Create 4 mechanical failure effects: 1) Vertical jumps using translateY with instant transitions: [{prog:0.3, val:0}, {prog:0.3001, val:-30}, {prog:0.32, val:-30}, {prog:0.3201, val:0}] - no easing for mechanical feel. 2) Frame blacks as opacity cuts: [{prog:0.45, val:1}, {prog:0.4501, val:0}, {prog:0.46, val:0}, {prog:0.4601, val:1}]. 3) Registration loss with translateX shifts: sudden ±5-15px shifts held for 0.1-0.3s. 4) Film plane wobble using rotate: [{prog:0, val:0}, {prog:0.2, val:0.5}, {prog:0.4, val:-0.3}...] in small increments. 5) Tension variations using scaleY: 0.98-1.02 pulses. Input schema: z.object({ damageSeverity: z.enum(['minor', 'moderate', 'severe']), damageType: z.enum(['tears', 'stretching', 'missing']), jumpFrequency: z.number().min(0).max(10), registrationLoss: z.enum(['stable', 'loose', 'erratic']), duration: z.number(), targetIds: z.array(z.string()) }). PresetMetadata: { _internalPreset: true, _internalPresetOutput: 'effects' }

prompts.prompt: Build an internal combined effect preset 'VintageProjectionArtifacts' that layers multiple vintage film artifacts into a comprehensive aging system. Combine gate weave, focus hunting, exposure fluctuations, and edge vignetting into a cohesive vintage look. The effect should subtly combine horizontal weave (±2px), focus breathing (blur 0-1.5px), exposure pumping (brightness 0.95-1.05), and dynamic vignetting. Add a film grain texture overlay that changes intensity based on the exposure level (darker areas have more visible grain). Include parameters for projection quality (pristine/good/fair/poor), artifact intensity (0-1), grain visibility (0-1), and whether to include chromatic aberration. Effects should interact - when exposure drops, grain increases, when focus shifts, vignette softens.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Effect type: Combined Generic effects with interconnected animations. Create 6 interdependent effects: 1) Gate weave: translateX with slow sine wave pattern [{prog:0, val:0}, {prog:0.25, val:2}, {prog:0.5, val:0}, {prog:0.75, val:-2}, {prog:1, val:0}]. 2) Focus hunting: blur filter oscillating [{prog:0, val:0}, {prog:0.15, val:1}, {prog:0.3, val:0.5}, {prog:0.45, val:1.5}, {prog:0.6, val:0}...]. 3) Exposure pumping: brightness filter [{prog:0, val:1}, {prog:0.2, val:0.95}, {prog:0.4, val:1.05}, {prog:0.6, val:0.97}...]. 4) Dynamic vignette: radial-gradient opacity inversely tied to focus (more blur = softer vignette). 5) Grain intensity: opacity tied to brightness (lower brightness = higher grain opacity 0.05-0.15). 6) Optional chromatic aberration: RGB channel splits with slight offset. Input schema: z.object({ projectionQuality: z.enum(['pristine', 'good', 'fair', 'poor']), artifactIntensity: z.number().min(0).max(1), grainVisibility: z.number().min(0).max(1), includeChromaticAberration: z.boolean(), duration: z.number(), targetIds: z.array(z.string()) }). Return format: { effects: [...interconnected effects array] }
